"""Deployment gate (docs/03 "Deployment gate", ops/CONVENTIONS.md "Runtime configuration").

Local development binds loopback only. A non-loopback bind requires *explicitly
configured* authentication, TLS termination, secured session cookies, CSRF
protection, private object storage, a backup/purge (retention) policy, and a
consent configuration. Missing any control must refuse the bind (fail closed).
No implicit credentials such as ``admin/admin``.

The API server (Phase 12) must call :func:`assert_binding_allowed` before
binding any socket. DNS is deliberately not resolved here: an unresolvable or
unrecognized host fails closed as non-loopback.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import ipaddress
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

__all__ = [
    "DeploymentGateError",
    "DeploymentControls",
    "GateDecision",
    "assert_binding_allowed",
    "evaluate_binding",
    "is_loopback_host",
]

# Tokens that mean "a default/placeholder credential", not a configured secret.
# Substring matches catch composed defaults such as "admin/admin" or "changeme1".
PLACEHOLDER_CREDENTIAL_TOKENS: frozenset[str] = frozenset(
    {
        "admin",
        "administrator",
        "root",
        "password",
        "passwd",
        "changeme",
        "change_me",
        "default",
        "dev",
        "example",
        "fixme",
        "letmein",
        "none",
        "null",
        "placeholder",
        "sample",
        "secret",
        "test",
        "todo",
        "",
    }
)

LOOPBACK_HOSTNAMES: frozenset[str] = frozenset({"localhost"})


class DeploymentGateError(PermissionError):
    """Raised when a bind is refused by the deployment gate."""

    def __init__(self, unmet: tuple[str, ...]):
        self.unmet = unmet
        names = ", ".join(unmet)
        super().__init__(
            "Deployment gate: refusing non-loopback bind; unmet controls: "
            f"{names}. Configure them explicitly (docs/03 deployment gate) or "
            "bind to loopback for local demo mode."
        )


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class DeploymentControls:
    """Explicit deployment configuration. Every default is *unconfigured*."""

    auth_mechanism: str | None = None
    credential: str | None = None
    tls_termination: bool = False
    session_cookies_secured: bool = False
    csrf_protection: bool = False
    object_store_private: bool = False
    backup_expiry_configured: bool = False
    consent_configuration: str | None = None
    deployment_approved: bool = False


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class GateDecision:
    allowed: bool
    mode: str  # "local_demo" | "network"
    unmet: tuple[str, ...] = field(default_factory=tuple)


def _is_blank_or_placeholder(value: str | None) -> bool:
    """Exact-match check for configuration references (mechanism names, policy IDs)."""
    if value is None:
        return True
    return value.strip().lower() in PLACEHOLDER_CREDENTIAL_TOKENS


def _is_weak_credential(value: str | None) -> bool:
    """Credentials get the stricter rule: any embedded default token fails.

    Substring matching catches composed defaults such as "admin/admin" or
    "changeme1"; it is deliberately applied to secrets only, so a policy file
    reference like "policies/consent-default.json" is not misflagged.
    """
    if _is_blank_or_placeholder(value):
        return True
    stripped = value.strip().lower()
    return any(token and token in stripped for token in PLACEHOLDER_CREDENTIAL_TOKENS)


def is_loopback_host(host: str) -> bool:
    """True only for explicit loopback addresses/names; unknown hosts fail closed."""
    candidate = host.strip().strip("[]").lower()
    if candidate in LOOPBACK_HOSTNAMES:
        return True
    try:
        return ipaddress.ip_address(candidate).is_loopback
    except ValueError:
        return False


def evaluate_binding(host: str, controls: DeploymentControls) -> GateDecision:
    """Decide whether ``host`` may be bound under ``controls``.

    Loopback binds are allowed for local development or configured local
    research. Any other host requires every control and explicit approval.
    """
    if is_loopback_host(host):
        return GateDecision(allowed=True, mode="local_demo", unmet=())
    unmet: list[str] = []
    if _is_blank_or_placeholder(controls.auth_mechanism):
        unmet.append("authentication")
    if _is_weak_credential(controls.credential):
        unmet.append("credentials_not_default")
    if not controls.tls_termination:
        unmet.append("tls_termination")
    if not controls.session_cookies_secured:
        unmet.append("session_cookies_secured")
    if not controls.csrf_protection:
        unmet.append("csrf_protection")
    if not controls.object_store_private:
        unmet.append("object_store_private")
    if not controls.backup_expiry_configured:
        unmet.append("backup_purge_policy")
    if _is_blank_or_placeholder(controls.consent_configuration):
        unmet.append("consent_configuration")
    if not controls.deployment_approved:
        unmet.append("deployment_approved")
    return GateDecision(allowed=not unmet, mode="network", unmet=tuple(unmet))


def assert_binding_allowed(host: str, controls: DeploymentControls) -> GateDecision:
    """Refuse (raise) unless ``host`` may be bound under ``controls``."""
    decision = evaluate_binding(host, controls)
    if not decision.allowed:
        raise DeploymentGateError(decision.unmet)
    return decision

"""Static outbound-network (egress) scan of repository code (D29, docs/15).

External inference, analytics, and telemetry default off. This scanner is a
repository-level regression gate: app/runtime code must not call out to the
network directly. Model downloads are configured separately (CONVENTIONS:
opt-in, hash-verified) and appear here as findings until a reviewed,
file-scoped allowlist entry exists. Literal offline-only model loaders and
reviewed, content-pinned loopback callables are distinguished from outbound
requests; entries may additionally require exact reviewed source bytes.

The scan reads tracked files only (``git ls-files``), so scratch files and
private runtime data are never inspected or reported by CI runs. It never
performs any network request itself.

Allowlist policy: entries are (relative path, pattern name) pairs with a
justification. A stale entry (file removed) fails the test suite, so the
allowlist cannot accumulate silently.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import ast
import hashlib
import re
import subprocess
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

__all__ = ["ALLOWED_EGRESS", "EgressFinding", "scan_files", "scan_repository"]

_CODE_SUFFIXES = frozenset({".py", ".ts", ".tsx", ".js", ".jsx", ".mjs", ".sh", ".yml", ".yaml"})
# Documentation/prose trees may legitimately mention URLs and API names.
# labs/fold-studio/reports/ holds the imported lab's frozen evidence receipts
# (see labs/fold-studio/IMPORT_PROVENANCE.md): historical check scripts that
# are never executed by CI. Live lab code (labs/fold-studio/mvstudio,
# labs/fold-studio/scripts) remains fully scanned.

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EgressFinding:
    path: str
    line_no: int
    pattern: str
    snippet: str


# name -> compiled line pattern. Anchored to call/import shapes, not prose.
# Patterns are deliberately self-avoiding: they require the context they detect
# (real whitespace after "import", dotted usage, argument position) so this
# module's own source lines can never match once it is tracked.
_PATTERNS: tuple[tuple[str, re.Pattern[str]], ...] = (
    ("requests_library", re.compile(r"^\s*(import\s+requests|from\s+requests\s+import)\b|requests\.(get|post|put|patch|delete|head|options|request|Session)\(")),
    ("urllib", re.compile(r"\burllib\.request\b|\burlopen\s*\(")),
    ("raw_socket", re.compile(r"\bsocket\.socket\s*\(|\bsocket\.create_connection\b|\.\s*connect_ex\s*\(")),
    ("httpx_outbound", re.compile(r"\bhttpx\.(get|post|put|patch|delete|head|options|request|stream|Client)\s*\(")),
    ("aiohttp", re.compile(r"\b(?:import\s+aiohttp|from\s+aiohttp\s+import|aiohttp\.ClientSession)\b")),
    ("grpc", re.compile(r"\b(?:import\s+grpc|from\s+grpc\s+import)\b")),
    ("mail_ftp_telnet", re.compile(r"\b(?:import\s+(?:smtplib|ftplib|telnetlib))\b")),
    ("telemetry_sdk", re.compile(r"\b(?:import\s+(?:sentry_sdk|posthog|bugsnag|mixpanel)|from\s+(?:sentry_sdk|posthog|bugsnag|mixpanel)\s+import)\b|\b(?:sentry_sdk|posthog|bugsnag|mixpanel)\s*\.\s*\w+\s*\(")),

ALLOWLIST_SOURCE_SHA256 = {

# Reviewed callable ASTs, not path-wide exemptions. A changed guard or a new
# outbound call outside these callables remains a finding. Imports are pinned
# with the study guard because they choose the redirect/proxy implementations.
_LOOPBACK_GUARDS = {

def _local_loader_lines(tree: ast.Module) -> set[int]:
    safe, unsafe = set(), set()
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if not isinstance(node, ast.Call):
            continue
        name = node.func.attr if isinstance(node.func, ast.Attribute) else (
            node.func.id if isinstance(node.func, ast.Name) else None)
        if name not in {"from_pretrained", "hf_hub_download", "snapshot_download"}:
            continue
        local = name == "from_pretrained" and any(
            kw.arg == "local_files_only" and isinstance(kw.value, ast.Constant)
            and kw.value.value is True for kw in node.keywords)
        (safe if local else unsafe).add(node.lineno)
    return safe - unsafe


def _loopback_lines(tree: ast.Module, path: str) -> set[int]:
    rule = _LOOPBACK_GUARDS.get(path)
    if rule is None:
        return set()
    names, digest = rule
    nodes = [n for n in tree.body if isinstance(n, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.ClassDef))
             and n.name in names]
    if path == "research/study/backends.py":
        nodes += [n for n in tree.body if isinstance(n, ast.ImportFrom)
                  and n.module == "urllib" + ".request"]
    source = ast.dump(ast.Module(body=nodes, type_ignores=[]), include_attributes=False)
    if hashlib.sha256(source.encode()).hexdigest() != digest:
        return set()
    return {line for n in nodes for line in range(n.lineno, n.end_lineno + 1)}


def _tracked_files(root: Path) -> list[Path]:
    proc = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "ls-files", "-z"], cwd=root, capture_output=True, check=True
    )
    names = [n for n in proc.stdout.decode().split("\0") if n]
    files = []
    for name in names:
        if not name.endswith(tuple(_CODE_SUFFIXES)):
            continue
        if name.startswith(_SKIPPED_PREFIXES):
            continue
        path = root / name
        if path.is_file():
            files.append(path)
    return files


def scan_files(paths: list[Path], *, root: Path | None = None) -> list[EgressFinding]:
    """Scan explicit files (used for injected fixtures and repository scans)."""
    findings: list[EgressFinding] = []
    for path in paths:
        try:
            lines = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
        except (UnicodeDecodeError, OSError):
            continue
        for line_no, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
            for name, pattern in _PATTERNS:
                if pattern.search(line):
                    findings.append(
                        EgressFinding(
                            path=str(path.relative_to(root) if root else path),
                            line_no=line_no,
                            pattern=name,
                            snippet=line.strip()[:200],
                        )
                    )
    return findings


def scan_repository(root: Path) -> list[EgressFinding]:
    """Scan tracked code; suppress only verified local calls/guarded scopes.

    Suppression is the conjunction of both review mechanisms where they
    overlap: an entry is dropped only when its allowlist tuple matches, its
    file pin (when present) matches the exact reviewed bytes, and the call
    passes the applicable AST check (literal offline-only loaders, or the
    pinned loopback callables).
    """
    findings = []
    parsed: dict[str, tuple[set[int], set[int]]] = {}
    for finding in scan_files(_tracked_files(root), root=root):
        if finding.path not in parsed:
            try:
                tree = ast.parse((root / finding.path).read_text())
                parsed[finding.path] = (_local_loader_lines(tree), _loopback_lines(tree, finding.path))
            except (SyntaxError, UnicodeError, OSError):
                parsed[finding.path] = (set(), set())
        local_lines, guarded_lines = parsed[finding.path]
        pin = ALLOWLIST_SOURCE_SHA256.get(finding.path)
        file_pinned = pin is None or hashlib.sha256(
            (root / finding.path).read_bytes()).hexdigest() == pin
        # Pinned loopback callables suppress their own urllib/httpx lines
        # without an allowlist entry: the study backend guard pins imports and
        # callables directly and predates the file-scoped allowlist. A file
        # that carries a source pin must satisfy BOTH mechanisms — any edited
        # byte invalidates the whole exception.
        if (finding.pattern in {"urllib", "httpx_outbound"}
                and finding.line_no in guarded_lines and file_pinned):
            continue
        if (finding.path, finding.pattern) in ALLOWED_EGRESS:
            ast_ok = (
                (finding.pattern == "model_hub_download" and finding.line_no in local_lines)
                or (finding.pattern in {"urllib", "httpx_outbound"}
                    and finding.path not in _LOOPBACK_GUARDS)
                or finding.pattern not in {"model_hub_download", "urllib", "httpx_outbound"}
            )
            if file_pinned and ast_ok:
                continue
        findings.append(finding)
    return findings

"""Safe API error envelope (docs/03 "API contract", ops/CONVENTIONS.md).

Error JSON must be exactly ``{code, message, correlation_id, retryable}``:
- ``code``: short lowercase machine-readable token.
- ``message``: safe human text. Never a stack trace, storage path, transcript,
  connection string, or credential. Single line, bounded length.
- ``correlation_id``: opaque per-request identifier for log correlation.
- ``retryable``: bool.

Unknown fields fail closed (docs/04), so the validator rejects extra keys.
Phase 12 must route every HTTP error through :func:`safe_error`; unhandled
framework errors must be converted by a final exception handler before they
reach a client.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
from typing import Any

__all__ = [
    "ERROR_KEYS",
    "ERROR_MESSAGE_CATALOG",
    "MAX_SAFE_MESSAGE_LENGTH",
    "ErrorEnvelopeError",
    "leak_indicators",
    "sanitize_message",
    "safe_error",
    "validate_error_envelope",
]

ERROR_KEYS = frozenset({"code", "message", "correlation_id", "retryable"})

# The binding control against transcripts/stack traces in responses: error
# messages are developer-authored static catalog text keyed by code. Callers
# that omit ``message`` get the catalog entry; a custom message is a reviewed
# exception and still passes the structural leak checks below.
#
# Phase 12 per-code binding (backend worker): the second block binds the API
# error vocabulary (services/api/app/errors.py ``STATUS_BY_CODE``) so every
# ``ApiError`` code has a catalog entry. The API's envelope builder routes
# through :func:`safe_error`, and services/api/app/errors.py fails fast at
# import when an API code is missing here — adding a code without catalog
# text cannot ship. Raise sites may still pass reviewed static text; the
# catalog entry is the default and the leak-checked backstop either way.
ERROR_MESSAGE_CATALOG: dict[str, str] = {
    "bad_request": "The request could not be parsed.",
    "asset_not_found": "The requested asset is not available in this project.",
    "object_not_found": "The requested object is not available in this project.",
    "version_conflict": "The object changed since you loaded it; reload and retry.",
    "payload_too_large": "Upload exceeds the configured size limit.",
    "unsupported_media_type": "This media type is not accepted.",
    "capture_too_long": "Recording exceeds the configured duration limit.",
    "archive_refused": "Archive uploads are not accepted in v0.1.",
    "schema_invalid": "The submitted record does not match the schema.",
    "not_authorized": "You do not have access to this object.",
    "rate_limited": "Too many requests; retry later.",
    "provider_unavailable": "A required analysis provider is unavailable.",
    "internal_error": "Internal error (details withheld; reference the correlation ID).",
    # --- API vocabulary (services/api/app/errors.py STATUS_BY_CODE) ---
    "not_found": "The requested object is not available in your scope.",
    "unauthorized": "Authentication is required for this request.",
    "forbidden_scope": "You do not have access to this object.",
    "research_export_not_authorized": (
        "This account does not hold explicit research-export permission."
    ),
    "conflict": "The request conflicts with the current state; reload and retry.",
    "unprocessable_entity": "The submitted record does not match the schema.",
    "range_not_satisfiable": "The requested byte range is outside this asset.",
    "unavailable": "A required backing service is temporarily unavailable.",
}

# Proposed engineering bound: a safe message is one short line. Stack traces and
# transcripts are far longer; the cap makes accidental passthrough detectable.
MAX_SAFE_MESSAGE_LENGTH = 512

_CODE_RE = re.compile(r"^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_.-]{0,63}$")
_CORRELATION_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,64}$")

# Indicators that a string carries internal detail that must not reach a client.
_LEAK_PATTERNS: tuple[tuple[str, re.Pattern[str]], ...] = (
    ("stack_trace_header", re.compile(r"Traceback \(most recent call last\)")),
    ("source_location", re.compile(r"File \"[^\"]+\", line \d+")),
    ("source_file_suffix", re.compile(r"\.py\b")),
    ("absolute_path", re.compile(r"(^|[\s\"'=(])((?:/[^/\s\"']+){2,}|[A-Za-z]:\\\\[^\"'\s]+)")),
    ("sql_text", re.compile(r"\b(SELECT .+ FROM|INSERT INTO|UPDATE .+ SET|DELETE FROM)\b", re.IGNORECASE)),
    ("connection_url", re.compile(r"\b(postgresql(\+\w+)?|redis|mysql|mongodb)://\S+", re.IGNORECASE)),
    ("bearer_token", re.compile(r"\bBearer\s+\S+", re.IGNORECASE)),
    ("api_token_shape", re.compile(r"\b(gh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{10,}|sk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}|AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|xoxb-[0-9A-Za-z-]{10,})\b")),
    ("private_key_block", re.compile(r"-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----")),
    ("keyword_value_pair", re.compile(r"\b(password|api[_-]?key|secret|token)\s*[:=]", re.IGNORECASE)),
)


class ErrorEnvelopeError(ValueError):
    """Raised when an error payload violates the safe error contract."""

    def __init__(self, violations: tuple[str, ...]):
        self.violations = violations
        super().__init__("Unsafe error payload: " + "; ".join(violations))


def leak_indicators(text: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """Names of leak patterns present in ``text`` (empty when safe)."""
    if not isinstance(text, str):
        return ("not_a_string",)
    found = [name for name, pattern in _LEAK_PATTERNS if pattern.search(text)]
    if "\n" in text or "\r" in text:
        found.append("multiline_text")
    if len(text) > MAX_SAFE_MESSAGE_LENGTH:
        found.append("message_too_long")
    return tuple(found)


def sanitize_message(raw: str) -> str:
    """Return a client-safe message; internal detail is withheld, not trimmed."""
    if leak_indicators(raw):
        return "Internal error (details withheld; reference the correlation ID)."
    return raw


def validate_error_envelope(payload: Any) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """Return violation names for ``payload`` (empty tuple when contract-safe).

    Reviewed exception (lead, 2026-09-30, F-03 reconciliation): a schema-validation
    422 may carry one extra key, ``details``, holding ONLY field locators — each
    item must be an object with a list-of-strings ``loc`` and a string ``msg``.
    Raw input values, stack text, or any other shape fail closed.
    """
    violations: list[str] = []
    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
        return ("not_an_object",)
    keys = set(payload)
    allowed = set(ERROR_KEYS) | {"details"}
    if not keys <= allowed or not set(ERROR_KEYS) <= keys:
        missing = sorted(ERROR_KEYS - keys)
        extra = sorted(keys - allowed)
        if missing:
            violations.append("missing_keys:" + ",".join(missing))
        if extra:
            violations.append("unknown_keys_fail_closed:" + ",".join(extra))
        return tuple(violations)
    if not isinstance(payload["code"], str) or not _CODE_RE.match(payload["code"]):
        violations.append("invalid_code")
    if not isinstance(payload["correlation_id"], str) or not _CORRELATION_RE.match(payload["correlation_id"]):
        violations.append("invalid_correlation_id")
    if not isinstance(payload["retryable"], bool):
        violations.append("retryable_not_boolean")
    message = payload["message"]
    if not isinstance(message, str) or not message.strip():
        violations.append("empty_message")
    else:
        violations.extend(f"leak:{name}" for name in leak_indicators(message))
    details = payload.get("details")
    if details is not None:
        if not isinstance(details, list) or not details:
            violations.append("details_not_nonempty_list")
        else:
            for item in details:
                if not isinstance(item, dict) or set(item) != {"loc", "msg"}:
                    violations.append("details_item_shape")
                    continue
                loc, msg = item["loc"], item["msg"]
                if not (isinstance(loc, list) and all(isinstance(p, str) for p in loc)):
                    violations.append("details_loc_not_string_list")
                if not isinstance(msg, str):
                    violations.append("details_msg_not_string")
                else:
                    violations.extend(
                        f"details_leak:{name}" for name in leak_indicators(msg))
    return tuple(violations)


def safe_error(
    *,
    code: str,
    correlation_id: str,
    retryable: bool,
    message: str | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Build a contract-safe error envelope; raises if the result is unsafe.

    ``message`` defaults to the static catalog entry for ``code`` so dynamic
    content (exception text, transcripts, paths) never reaches a client by
    default. An explicit message is leak-checked as a backstop.
    """
    chosen = ERROR_MESSAGE_CATALOG.get(code, ERROR_MESSAGE_CATALOG["internal_error"]) \
        if message is None else sanitize_message(message)
    envelope = {
        "code": code,
        "message": chosen,
        "correlation_id": correlation_id,
        "retryable": bool(retryable),
    }
    violations = validate_error_envelope(envelope)
    if violations:
        raise ErrorEnvelopeError(violations)
    return envelope

"""Media path and filename policy (docs/15 "Media and agent isolation").

Rules enforced here, all fail closed:
- A user-supplied filename is display text only. It is never used to derive a
  storage path (docs/03; ops/CONVENTIONS.md "no path derivation from user
  filenames"). Storage keys come from opaque asset IDs plus content hash.
- Path traversal, absolute paths, separator and control characters, Windows
  drive/reserved names, and shell metacharacters are rejected in filenames.
- Symlink escapes out of a storage root are rejected.
- Archive uploads are refused in v0.1 (no client-side archive extraction).

The media decode sandbox itself (network off, non-root, read-only input,
output quota, memory/time limits, pinned decoder) is a Phase 04 worker
responsibility; this module is the path boundary in front of it.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
import unicodedata
from pathlib import Path

__all__ = [
    "PathPolicyError",
    "ARCHIVE_SUFFIXES",
    "assert_opaque_id",
    "assert_symlink_safe",
    "reject_archives",
    "storage_key",
    "validate_display_filename",
]

_MAX_FILENAME_BYTES = 255
_MAX_OPAQUE_ID_LENGTH = 64
_OPAQUE_ID_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$")
_SHA256_RE = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-f]{64}$")
_WINDOWS_DRIVE_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z]:")
# Case-insensitive Windows reserved device names, with or without extension.
_RESERVED_NAMES = frozenset(
    {"con", "prn", "aux", "nul"}
    | {f"com{i}" for i in range(1, 10)}
    | {f"lpt{i}" for i in range(1, 10)}
)
# Shell metacharacters: filenames never reach a shell, and keeping them out of
# names removes a whole class of downstream interpolation mistakes.
_SHELL_METACHARACTERS = frozenset(';|&$`<>\\"\'!{}[]()')
# v0.1 refuses archive uploads entirely; media normalization is a derivative
# produced by the worker, not client-supplied extraction.
ARCHIVE_SUFFIXES = frozenset(
    {".zip", ".tar", ".gz", ".tgz", ".bz2", ".xz", ".7z", ".rar", ".jar", ".war"}
)

_ALLOWED_KEY_SUFFIXES = frozenset(
    {".mp4", ".webm", ".mov", ".wav", ".mp3", ".m4a", ".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png", ".json", ".bin"}
)


class PathPolicyError(ValueError):
    """Raised when a path, filename, or identifier violates policy."""

    def __init__(self, code: str, detail: str):
        self.code = code
        super().__init__(f"{code}: {detail}")


def validate_display_filename(name: str) -> str:
    """Validate a user-supplied filename for display/storage metadata use."""
    if not name or not name.strip():
        raise PathPolicyError("empty_filename", "filename is empty")
    if len(name.encode("utf-8")) > _MAX_FILENAME_BYTES:
        raise PathPolicyError("filename_too_long", "filename exceeds 255 UTF-8 bytes")
    if name in (".", ".."):
        raise PathPolicyError("path_traversal", "dot filenames are refused")
    if _WINDOWS_DRIVE_RE.match(name):
        raise PathPolicyError("windows_drive", "filenames must not carry a drive prefix")
    if "/" in name or "\\" in name:
        raise PathPolicyError("path_separator", "filenames must not contain path separators")
    if name.startswith("-"):
        raise PathPolicyError("option_like", "filenames must not start with '-'")
    stem = name.split(".", 1)[0].strip().lower()
    if stem in _RESERVED_NAMES:
        raise PathPolicyError("reserved_device_name", "Windows reserved device name")
    for char in name:
        if unicodedata.category(char) in ("Cc", "Cf"):
            raise PathPolicyError(
                "control_or_format_character",
                "filenames must not contain control or format characters",
            )
        if char in _SHELL_METACHARACTERS:
            raise PathPolicyError("shell_metacharacter", f"refused character in filename")
    if name != name.strip(" ."):
        raise PathPolicyError("padding_characters", "leading/trailing spaces or dots are refused")
    return name


def reject_archives(name: str) -> str:
    """Refuse archive uploads (v0.1 has no archive extraction path)."""
    suffixes = [s for s in Path(name).suffixes if s.lower() in ARCHIVE_SUFFIXES]
    if suffixes:
        raise PathPolicyError(
            "archive_refused",
            "v0.1 refuses archive uploads; provide individual media files",
        )
    return name


def assert_opaque_id(identifier: str, *, kind: str = "id") -> str:
    """Opaque IDs are short charset-bounded tokens; they never carry path syntax."""
    if not identifier or not _OPAQUE_ID_RE.match(identifier):
        raise PathPolicyError("opaque_id_invalid", f"{kind} is not an opaque identifier")
    if len(identifier) > _MAX_OPAQUE_ID_LENGTH:
        raise PathPolicyError("opaque_id_invalid", f"{kind} exceeds 64 characters")
    return identifier


def storage_key(asset_id: str, sha256: str, suffix: str) -> str:
    """Derive an internal storage key from opaque ID + content hash only.

    ``suffix`` must be a known lowercase media/metadata extension with the
    leading dot. The user filename is deliberately not an input.
    """
    assert_opaque_id(asset_id, kind="asset_id")
    if not _SHA256_RE.match(sha256):
        raise PathPolicyError("content_hash_invalid", "sha256 must be 64 lowercase hex chars")
    normalized = suffix.lower()
    if normalized not in _ALLOWED_KEY_SUFFIXES:
        raise PathPolicyError("storage_suffix_refused", f"suffix {normalized!r} is not allowed")
    return f"assets/{asset_id}/{sha256}{normalized}"


def assert_symlink_safe(root: Path, relative: Path) -> Path:
    """Resolve ``relative`` under ``root`` and refuse traversal or symlink escape.

    Every existing component is checked for being a symlink; the final resolved
    path must remain inside the resolved root.
    """
    if relative.is_absolute():
        raise PathPolicyError("absolute_path", "storage paths are root-relative")
    root_resolved = root.resolve()
    current = root_resolved
    for part in relative.parts:
        if part in (".", ""):
            continue
        if part == "..":
            raise PathPolicyError("path_traversal", "'..' is refused")
        current = current / part
        if current.is_symlink():
            raise PathPolicyError("symlink_escape", f"symlinked component {part!r} is refused")
    resolved = current.resolve()
    if resolved != root_resolved and root_resolved not in resolved.parents:
        raise PathPolicyError("path_escape", "resolved path leaves the storage root")
    return resolved


def ensure_directory(root: Path, relative: Path) -> Path:
    """Create (if needed) and return a policy-checked directory under ``root``.

    The only filesystem-writing helper in this package, for storage setup code
    that must respect the same boundary.
    """
    resolved = assert_symlink_safe(root, relative)
    resolved.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return resolved

"""Retention and deletion policy (docs/15 "Data minimization and retention").

Numbers are proposed local-pilot policy defaults, not legal requirements; an
approved research policy may supersede them explicitly. On withdrawal or
deletion, access is revoked immediately, active-store derivatives, jobs,
caches, and answers purge within the engineering target, and backup expiry
must be configured and verified before any external deployment.

The Phase 12 purge job must import :data:`REQUIRED_PURGE_TARGETS` and
:func:`assert_purge_plan_complete` so a purge plan cannot silently omit a
record family.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Iterable

__all__ = [
    "PROPOSED_RAW_CAPTURE_RETENTION_DAYS",
    "PROPOSED_DERIVED_ANALYSIS_RETENTION_DAYS",
    "PROPOSED_ACTIVE_PURGE_TARGET_MINUTES",
    "REQUIRED_PURGE_TARGETS",
    "WITHDRAWAL_SEQUENCE",
    "RetentionConfigError",
    "assert_purge_plan_complete",
    "validate_retention_config",
    "validate_withdrawal_sequence",
]

# docs/15: "raw capture retention 30 days and derived analysis 90 days unless an
# approved research policy explicitly supersedes them"; "purge within a
# 15-minute engineering target".
PROPOSED_RAW_CAPTURE_RETENTION_DAYS = 30
PROPOSED_DERIVED_ANALYSIS_RETENTION_DAYS = 90
PROPOSED_ACTIVE_PURGE_TARGET_MINUTES = 15

# Deletion/withdrawal must reach every record family: originals (raw bytes),
# derivatives (thumbnails, keyframes, transcripts, crops), embeddings,
# processing jobs, cached/derived answers (invalidated, not served), and
# research exports.
REQUIRED_PURGE_TARGETS: tuple[str, ...] = (
    "originals",
    "derivatives",
    "embeddings",
    "processing_jobs",
    "answers",
    "research_exports",
)

WITHDRAWAL_SEQUENCE: tuple[str, ...] = ("revoke_access", "purge_active_store", "expire_backups")


class RetentionConfigError(ValueError):
    """Raised when retention configuration or a purge plan fails policy."""


def assert_purge_plan_complete(targets: Iterable[str]) -> None:
    """Refuse a purge plan that omits any required record family."""
    planned = set(targets)
    missing = [name for name in REQUIRED_PURGE_TARGETS if name not in planned]
    if missing:
        raise RetentionConfigError(
            "Incomplete purge plan; missing record families: " + ", ".join(missing)
        )
    unknown = sorted(planned - set(REQUIRED_PURGE_TARGETS))
    if unknown:
        raise RetentionConfigError("Unknown purge targets: " + ", ".join(unknown))


def validate_withdrawal_sequence(steps: Iterable[str]) -> None:
    """Access revocation must precede active-store purge, which precedes backups."""
    planned = list(steps)
    missing = [s for s in WITHDRAWAL_SEQUENCE if s not in set(planned)]
    present = [s for s in planned if s in WITHDRAWAL_SEQUENCE]
    expected = [s for s in WITHDRAWAL_SEQUENCE if s in set(planned)]
    if missing:
        raise RetentionConfigError(
            "Withdrawal sequence is missing steps: " + ", ".join(missing)
        )
    if present != expected:
        raise RetentionConfigError(
            "Withdrawal must revoke access before purging the active store and "
            "before relying on backup expiry"
        )


def validate_retention_config(
    *,
    backup_expiry_configured: bool,
    raw_capture_retention_days: int | None = None,
    derived_analysis_retention_days: int | None = None,
    active_purge_target_minutes: int | None = None,
    superseded_by_approved_policy: str | None = None,
) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """Return unmet retention controls (empty when compliant, fail closed).

    Retention windows longer than the proposed defaults require a reference to
    an explicitly approved superseding research policy.
    """
    unmet: list[str] = []
    if not backup_expiry_configured:
        unmet.append("backup_expiry_not_configured")
    extensions = {
        "raw_capture_retention_extended": (
            raw_capture_retention_days is not None
            and raw_capture_retention_days > PROPOSED_RAW_CAPTURE_RETENTION_DAYS
        ),
        "derived_analysis_retention_extended": (
            derived_analysis_retention_days is not None
            and derived_analysis_retention_days > PROPOSED_DERIVED_ANALYSIS_RETENTION_DAYS
        ),
        "purge_target_extended": (
            active_purge_target_minutes is not None
            and active_purge_target_minutes > PROPOSED_ACTIVE_PURGE_TARGET_MINUTES
        ),
    }
    if any(extensions.values()) and not (superseded_by_approved_policy or "").strip():
        unmet.extend(sorted(name for name, exceeded in extensions.items() if exceeded))
    return tuple(unmet)

_DEFAULTS = RuntimeCapabilities()


def load_capabilities(path: Path) -> RuntimeCapabilities:
    """Load capability flags; a missing file keeps the safe defaults visible."""
    try:
        raw = json.loads(Path(path).read_text())
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
        return _DEFAULTS
    known = {f: raw[f] for f in _DEFAULTS.__dataclass_fields__ if f in raw}
    return RuntimeCapabilities(**known)


@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def get_settings() -> Settings:
    return Settings()


@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def get_capabilities() -> RuntimeCapabilities:
    return capabilities_for_settings(get_settings())


def capabilities_for_settings(settings: Settings) -> RuntimeCapabilities:
    """Resolve this application's config and explicit fixture boundary.

    MV_FIXTURE_MODE is a deployment fact. Both true and false must override
    the dataclass default; otherwise analysis runs keep the fixture label.
    An app factory's supplied settings must never read another app's cache.
    """
    return replace(load_capabilities(settings.config_path), fixture_mode=settings.fixture_mode)


def reset_cached_settings() -> None:
    """Test/worker hook: drop cached settings after environment changes."""
    get_settings.cache_clear()
    get_capabilities.cache_clear()

"""Typed error envelope.

Every failure returns ``{code, message, correlation_id, retryable}``
(ops/CONVENTIONS.md). Messages are safe summaries; stack traces, storage
paths, and raw transcripts never enter the envelope.

Phase 12 per-code binding: every code in ``STATUS_BY_CODE`` MUST have an
entry in the static safe-message catalog (security/error_contract.py). The
import-time check below makes an unbound code a startup failure instead of a
runtime ``internal_error`` fallback with withheld context.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

from security.error_contract import ERROR_MESSAGE_CATALOG

STATUS_BY_CODE = {
    "not_found": 404,
    "unauthorized": 401,
    "forbidden_scope": 403,
    "research_export_not_authorized": 403,
    "conflict": 409,
    "payload_too_large": 413,
    "unsupported_media_type": 415,
    "unprocessable_entity": 422,
    "range_not_satisfiable": 416,
    "unavailable": 503,
    "internal_error": 500,
}

RETRYABLE_BY_DEFAULT = {"unavailable": True}


def assert_all_codes_bound(catalog: dict[str, str]) -> None:
    """Fail fast when an API code has no static catalog entry.

    Executed at import so an unbound code is a startup failure instead of a
    runtime ``internal_error`` fallback with withheld context.
    """
    missing = [code for code in STATUS_BY_CODE if code not in catalog]
    if missing:
        raise ImportError(
            "API error codes missing a safe-message catalog entry"
            " (security/error_contract.py ERROR_MESSAGE_CATALOG):"
            f" {', '.join(sorted(missing))}"
        )


assert_all_codes_bound(ERROR_MESSAGE_CATALOG)


def catalog_message(code: str) -> str:
    """The reviewed static text for ``code`` (safe_error's default)."""
    return ERROR_MESSAGE_CATALOG.get(code, ERROR_MESSAGE_CATALOG["internal_error"])


class ApiError(Exception):
    """A typed, safely renderable API failure."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        code: str,
        message: str,
        *,
        status: int | None = None,
        retryable: bool | None = None,
        details: list[Any] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(message)
        if code not in STATUS_BY_CODE and status is None:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown error code without explicit status: {code}")
        self.code = code
        self.message = message
        self.status = status if status is not None else STATUS_BY_CODE[code]
        self.retryable = (
            RETRYABLE_BY_DEFAULT.get(code, False) if retryable is None else retryable
        )
        self.details = details


def not_found(message: str = "No such object in your scope") -> ApiError:

"""FastAPI application factory (docs/03 service interfaces).

Every response carries correlation and capability headers. Every error uses
the typed envelope ``{code, message, correlation_id, retryable}`` with the
status codes specified in docs/03 (404 inaccessible, 409 conflict, 413 size,
415 type, 416 bad range, 422 schema/domain, 503 unavailable provider).

The engine and object store are created lazily on first request so importing
this module has no filesystem side effects. Non-loopback binds are refused
at factory time without the docs/03 deployment controls.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import re
import uuid
from pathlib import Path

from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.exceptions import RequestValidationError
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles
from starlette.exceptions import HTTPException as StarletteHTTPException

from security.deployment_gate import assert_binding_allowed
from security.error_contract import (
    ErrorEnvelopeError,
    safe_error,
    validate_error_envelope,
)

from .config import RuntimeCapabilities, Settings, capabilities_for_settings, get_settings
from .errors import ApiError
from .routers import authentication, checkpoints, fold_studio, guidance, longitudinal, media, projects, session, study
from .security import deployment_controls_from_settings, validate_authentication_settings

log = logging.getLogger("mv.api")

API_PREFIX = "/api/v1"

_CORRELATION_OK = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,64}$")


def _envelope(
    *,
    code: str,
    message: str | None,
    correlation_id: str,
    retryable: bool,
    status: int,
    details: list | None = None,
) -> JSONResponse:
    """Build the contract-safe error envelope (docs/03, Phase 12 binding).

    Every HTTP error is routed through ``safe_error``: an omitted message
    falls back to the per-code catalog entry, and any explicit raise-site
    message passes the structural leak checks before it can reach a client.
    A client-supplied correlation id that violates the envelope shape is
    replaced server-side rather than echoed into an invalid envelope.
    """
    if not _CORRELATION_OK.match(correlation_id or ""):
        correlation_id = uuid.uuid4().hex
    body = safe_error(
        code=code,
        correlation_id=correlation_id,
        retryable=retryable,
        message=message,
    )
    if details:
        body["details"] = details
        violations = validate_error_envelope(body)
        if violations:
            raise ErrorEnvelopeError(violations)
    return JSONResponse(status_code=status, content=body)


def _register_error_handlers(target: FastAPI) -> None:
    @target.exception_handler(ApiError)
    async def handle_api_error(request: Request, exc: ApiError):
        return _envelope(
            code=exc.code,
            message=exc.message,
            correlation_id=getattr(request.state, "correlation_id", ""),
            retryable=exc.retryable,
            status=exc.status,
            details=exc.details,
        )

    @target.exception_handler(RequestValidationError)
    async def handle_validation(request: Request, exc: RequestValidationError):
        details = [
            {"loc": [str(p) for p in err.get("loc", [])], "msg": str(err.get("msg", ""))}
            for err in exc.errors()
        ]
        return _envelope(
            code="unprocessable_entity",
            message="Request failed schema validation",
            correlation_id=getattr(request.state, "correlation_id", ""),
            retryable=False,
            status=422,
            details=details,
        )

    @target.exception_handler(StarletteHTTPException)
    async def handle_http_exception(request: Request, exc: StarletteHTTPException):
        code_map = {
            401: "unauthorized",
            404: "not_found",
            405: "not_found",
            409: "conflict",
            413: "payload_too_large",
            415: "unsupported_media_type",
            416: "range_not_satisfiable",
            422: "unprocessable_entity",
            503: "unavailable",
        }
        code = code_map.get(exc.status_code, "internal_error")
        return _envelope(
            code=code,
            message=str(exc.detail) if exc.detail else None,
            correlation_id=getattr(request.state, "correlation_id", ""),
            retryable=code == "unavailable",
            status=exc.status_code,
        )

    @target.exception_handler(Exception)
    async def handle_unexpected(request: Request, exc: Exception):
        log.error("unhandled error type=%s", type(exc).__name__)
        return _envelope(
            code="internal_error",
            message=None,  # catalog entry: details withheld, correlation only
            correlation_id=getattr(request.state, "correlation_id", ""),
            retryable=False,
            status=500,
        )


def create_app(
    settings: Settings | None = None,
    capabilities: RuntimeCapabilities | None = None,
    session_factory=None,
) -> FastAPI:
    """Build the application. Tests pass explicit settings and a session
    factory bound to their transactional SQLite database."""
    settings = settings or get_settings()
    # Factory-time deployment gate (threat model A7, THREAT_MODEL section 9):
    # loopback is always allowed; any other host requires every docs/03
    # control, none of which this process can configure yet. Fail closed.
    assert_binding_allowed(settings.host, deployment_controls_from_settings(settings))
    validate_authentication_settings(settings)
    capabilities = capabilities or capabilities_for_settings(settings)

    app = FastAPI(
        title="Making Visible API",
        version="0.1.0",
        docs_url="/api/docs",
        openapi_url="/api/openapi.json",
    )
    app.state.settings = settings
    app.state.capabilities = capabilities
    app.state.session_factory = session_factory  # built lazily when None
    app.state.object_store = None  # built lazily on first media access

    @app.middleware("http")
    async def correlation_and_capabilities(request: Request, call_next):
        # A client-supplied correlation id must satisfy the envelope shape or
        # it is replaced server-side; header and body always agree.
        supplied = request.headers.get("X-MV-Correlation-Id") or ""
        correlation_id = supplied if _CORRELATION_OK.match(supplied) else uuid.uuid4().hex
        request.state.correlation_id = correlation_id
        response = await call_next(request)
        response.headers["X-MV-Correlation-Id"] = correlation_id
        response.headers["X-MV-Authentication-Mode"] = settings.authentication_mode
        for name, value in request.app.state.capabilities.as_response_headers().items():
            response.headers[name] = value
        return response

    _register_error_handlers(app)

    # A single app carries the routes under /api/v1 (no mounted sub-app:
    # sub-apps own their state and dependency overrides, which would split
    # session factories and error handlers across two applications).
    app.include_router(projects.router, prefix=API_PREFIX)
    app.include_router(checkpoints.router, prefix=API_PREFIX)
    app.include_router(media.router, prefix=API_PREFIX)
    app.include_router(guidance.router, prefix=API_PREFIX)
    app.include_router(longitudinal.router, prefix=API_PREFIX)
    app.include_router(study.router, prefix=API_PREFIX)
    app.include_router(authentication.router, prefix=API_PREFIX)
    app.include_router(session.router, prefix=API_PREFIX)
    app.include_router(fold_studio.router, prefix=API_PREFIX)
    app.mount("/labs/fold-studio", StaticFiles(
        directory=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "labs/fold-studio/web", html=True,
    ), name="fold-studio")

    @app.get("/healthz")
    def healthz() -> dict:
        mode = "fixture" if app.state.capabilities.fixture_mode else "analysis"
        return {"status": "ok", "mode": mode}

    return app


def main() -> None:  # pragma: no cover - process entry
    import uvicorn

    from .db import create_engine, make_session_factory
    from .objectstore import store_from_settings

    settings = get_settings()
    app = create_app(settings)
    app.state.session_factory = make_session_factory(create_engine(settings))
    app.state.object_store = store_from_settings(settings)
    uvicorn.run(app, host=settings.host, port=settings.port, log_level="info", proxy_headers=False)


# uvicorn target for `make dev-host` (services.api.app.main:app). Import has
# no side effects beyond reading configuration; binding happens at startup.
# The binding gate validates Settings.host, which is authoritative in the
# supported launch paths (`make dev-host`, `python -m services.api.app.main`).
# A raw `uvicorn ... --host X` overrides the bind without changing Settings,
# so operators must not use it to expose the dev process beyond loopback.
app = create_app()

if __name__ == "__main__":  # pragma: no cover - process entry
    main()

"""Research login/session/logout; operator provisioning is outside this API."""
from __future__ import annotations

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Request, Response
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from ..db import as_aware
from ..dependencies import get_db
from ..dto import AuthenticationLogin, AuthenticationSessionResponse
from ..errors import ApiError
from ..security import CAPTURE_HEADER
from ..services import authentication as service

router = APIRouter()


def _check_route(request: Request) -> None:
    settings = request.app.state.settings
    if settings.authentication_mode != "research_session":
        raise ApiError("not_found", "Research authentication is not enabled")
    if settings.principal_header in request.headers or CAPTURE_HEADER in request.headers:
        raise ApiError("unauthorized", "Research authentication requires an unambiguous session")


def _response(authenticated: service.AuthenticatedSession) -> AuthenticationSessionResponse:
    return AuthenticationSessionResponse(
        principal_id=authenticated.row.principal_id,
        expires_at=as_aware(authenticated.row.expires_at),
        csrf_token=authenticated.csrf_token,
    )


@router.post("/auth/login", response_model=AuthenticationSessionResponse)
def login(
    payload: AuthenticationLogin,
    request: Request,
    response: Response,
    session: Session = Depends(get_db),
) -> AuthenticationSessionResponse:
    _check_route(request)
    settings = request.app.state.settings
    service.require_research_transport(request, settings, require_origin=True)
    authenticated = service.log_in(
        session, settings, payload.principal_id, payload.credential,
        prior_cookie=request.cookies.get(service.SESSION_COOKIE),
    )
    response.set_cookie(
        service.SESSION_COOKIE,
        authenticated.raw_session,
        max_age=settings.research_session_ttl_seconds,
        expires=as_aware(authenticated.row.expires_at),
        path="/",
        secure=True,
        httponly=True,
        samesite="strict",
    )
    response.headers["Cache-Control"] = "no-store"
    return _response(authenticated)


@router.get("/auth/session", response_model=AuthenticationSessionResponse)
def current_session(
    request: Request, response: Response, session: Session = Depends(get_db)
) -> AuthenticationSessionResponse:
    _check_route(request)
    authenticated = service.authenticate_session(request, session, request.app.state.settings)
    response.headers["Cache-Control"] = "no-store"
    return _response(authenticated)


@router.post("/auth/logout", status_code=204)
def logout(request: Request, session: Session = Depends(get_db)) -> Response:
    _check_route(request)
    authenticated = service.authenticate_session(request, session, request.app.state.settings)
    service.revoke_session(session, authenticated)
    response = Response(status_code=204, headers={"Cache-Control": "no-store"})
    response.delete_cookie(
        service.SESSION_COOKIE, path="/", secure=True, httponly=True, samesite="strict"
    )
    return response

@router.post("/projects/{project_id}/checkpoints", response_model=CheckpointResponse, status_code=201)

    payload: CheckpointCreate,
    principal: Principal = Depends(get_principal),
    session: Session = Depends(get_db),
    correlation_id: str = Depends(get_correlation_id),

    )
    audit_record(

        actor=principal.principal_id,
        action="checkpoint.created",
        object_type="checkpoint",
        object_id=checkpoint.id,
        project_id=project.id,
        detail={"phase": checkpoint.phase},
        correlation_id=correlation_id,

    session.flush()

@router.get("/checkpoints/{checkpoint_id}/setup", response_model=CheckpointSetupResponse)
def get_checkpoint_setup(
    checkpoint_id: str,
    principal: Principal = Depends(get_principal),
    session: Session = Depends(get_db),
) -> CheckpointSetupResponse:
    checkpoint = scoped_checkpoint(session, principal, checkpoint_id, CAPABILITY_READ)
    calibrations = session.execute(
        select(Calibration).where(
            Calibration.project_id == checkpoint.project_id,
            Calibration.checkpoint_id == checkpoint.id,
            Calibration.invalidated_at.is_(None),
        ).order_by(Calibration.created_at, Calibration.id)
    ).scalars().all()
    _, capabilities = project_with_caps(session, principal, checkpoint.project_id)
    visible = ["all", "teacher" if CAPABILITY_MANAGE in capabilities else "researcher"]
    associations = session.execute(
        select(ComponentAssociation).where(
            ComponentAssociation.project_id == checkpoint.project_id,
            ComponentAssociation.checkpoint_id == checkpoint.id,
            ComponentAssociation.status == "active",
            ComponentAssociation.visibility.in_(visible),
        ).order_by(ComponentAssociation.created_at, ComponentAssociation.id)
    ).scalars().all()
    return CheckpointSetupResponse(
        checkpoint=checkpoint_dto(checkpoint),
        calibrations=[calibration_dto(row) for row in calibrations],
        associations=[association_dto(row) for row in associations],
    )

@router.post("/checkpoints/{checkpoint_id}/uploads", response_model=UploadResponse, status_code=201)

    checkpoint_id: str,
    payload: UploadCreate,
    request: Request,
    principal: Principal = Depends(get_principal),
    session: Session = Depends(get_db),
) -> UploadResponse:
    """Stage an upload. Capture tokens may call this on their own checkpoint."""
    checkpoint = scoped_checkpoint(session, principal, checkpoint_id, CAPABILITY_UPLOAD)
    require_media_origin(request.app.state.settings, payload.origin)
    declaration = upload_service.UploadDeclaration(
        kind=payload.kind,
        content_type=payload.content_type,
        size_bytes=payload.size_bytes,
        sha256=payload.sha256,
        duration_ms=payload.duration_ms,
        width_px=payload.width_px,
        height_px=payload.height_px,
        audio_status=payload.audio_status,
        origin=payload.origin,
        original_name=payload.original_name,
        synthetic_manifest=payload.synthetic_manifest,
        privacy_class=payload.privacy_class,
        consent_use_flags=tuple(payload.consent_use_flags),
    )
    upload = upload_service.create_upload(
        session,
        checkpoint,
        declaration,
        actor=principal.principal_id,
        settings=request.app.state.settings,
    )
    return upload_dto(upload)


@router.put("/uploads/{upload_id}/content", response_model=UploadResponse)
async def put_upload_content(
    upload_id: str,
    request: Request,
    principal: Principal = Depends(get_principal),
    session: Session = Depends(get_db),
) -> UploadResponse:
    """Receive upload bytes. Size/type rules map to 413/415 (docs/03)."""
    upload = scoped_upload(session, principal, upload_id, CAPABILITY_UPLOAD)
    require_media_origin(request.app.state.settings, upload.origin)
    body = await request.body()
    upload_service.store_content(
        session,
        upload,
        body,
        content_type=request.headers.get("content-type"),
        settings=request.app.state.settings,
    )
    return upload_dto(upload)


@router.post("/uploads/{upload_id}/complete", response_model=UploadCompleteResponse, status_code=201)
def complete_upload(
    upload_id: str,
    request: Request,
    principal: Principal = Depends(get_principal),
    session: Session = Depends(get_db),
    store: ObjectStore = Depends(get_object_store),
    correlation_id: str = Depends(get_correlation_id),
) -> UploadCompleteResponse:
    """Finalize an upload into an immutable Asset (idempotent).

    Repeating complete, or finalizing identical bytes in the same checkpoint,
    returns the existing asset with ``idempotent_replay=true``.
    """
    upload = scoped_upload(session, principal, upload_id, CAPABILITY_UPLOAD)
    require_media_origin(request.app.state.settings, upload.origin)
    asset, replayed = upload_service.complete_upload(
        session,
        upload,
        store,
        actor=principal.principal_id,
        settings=request.app.state.settings,
    )
    audit_record(
        session,
        actor=principal.principal_id,
        action="upload.completed",
        object_type="asset",
        object_id=asset.id,
        project_id=asset.project_id,
        detail={"upload_id": upload.id, "replayed": replayed, "kind": asset.kind},
        correlation_id=correlation_id,
    )
    session.flush()
    return UploadCompleteResponse(
        asset=asset_dto(asset), idempotent_replay=replayed, upload=upload_dto(upload)
    )

@router.post("/checkpoints/{checkpoint_id}/analyze", response_model=AnalyzeResponse, status_code=202)
def analyze_checkpoint(
    checkpoint_id: str,
    payload: AnalyzeRequest,
    request: Request,
    principal: Principal = Depends(get_principal),
    session: Session = Depends(get_db),
    correlation_id: str = Depends(get_correlation_id),
) -> AnalyzeResponse:
    """Create idempotent analysis jobs and attempt queue delivery.

    Jobs persist in PostgreSQL regardless of dispatch; when Redis is absent
    the response reports a typed unavailable dispatch (202), not a fake run.
    """
    from ..services.analyzers import ANALYZER_ASSET_KINDS, REGISTRY, default_analysis_names

    checkpoint = scoped_checkpoint(session, principal, checkpoint_id, CAPABILITY_ANALYZE)
    assets = (
        session.query(Asset)
        .filter(
            Asset.checkpoint_id == checkpoint.id,
            Asset.project_id == checkpoint.project_id,
            Asset.status == "active",
        )
        .all()
    )
    if not assets:
        raise ApiError(
            "unprocessable_entity", "This checkpoint has no completed assets to analyze"
        )
    for asset in assets:
        require_media_origin(request.app.state.settings, asset.origin)
    requested = payload.analyzers or list(dict.fromkeys(
        name for asset in assets for name in default_analysis_names(
            asset, fixture_mode=request.app.state.capabilities.fixture_mode,
        )
    ))
    selected: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    for name in requested:
        versions = [v for (n, v) in REGISTRY if n == name]
        if not versions:
            raise ApiError(
                "unprocessable_entity", f"Analyzer {name!r} is not registered"
            )
        selected.append((name, versions[0]))

    parent_snapshot_hash = snapshots.current_snapshot_hash(session, checkpoint.project_id)
    jobs: list = []
    created_ids: list[str] = []
    dispatches: list[dict] = []
    for asset in assets:
        for analyzer_name, analyzer_version in selected:
            if asset.kind not in ANALYZER_ASSET_KINDS.get(analyzer_name, set()):
                continue
            if not payload.analyzers and analyzer_name not in default_analysis_names(
                asset, fixture_mode=request.app.state.capabilities.fixture_mode,
            ):
                continue
            config = job_service.analysis_configuration(session, checkpoint, asset, analyzer_name, payload.config)
            key = job_service.build_key(
                asset=asset,
                analyzer_name=analyzer_name,
                analyzer_version=analyzer_version,
                config=config,
                parent_snapshot_hash=parent_snapshot_hash,
            )
            job, created = job_service.get_or_create_job(
                session,
                project=checkpoint_scope_project(session, checkpoint),
                checkpoint=checkpoint,
                asset=asset,
                key=key,
                created_by=principal.principal_id,
                config=config,
            )
            jobs.append(job)
            if created:
                created_ids.append(job.id)
            dispatches.append(
                {
                    "job_id": job.id,
                    **job_service.dispatch(session, job, settings=request.app.state.settings),
                }
            )
    if not jobs:
        raise ApiError("unprocessable_entity", "No selected analyzer supports this checkpoint's asset kinds")
    audit_record(
        session,
        actor=principal.principal_id,
        action="checkpoint.analyze",
        object_type="checkpoint",
        object_id=checkpoint.id,
        project_id=checkpoint.project_id,
        detail={
            "jobs": [j.id for j in jobs],
            "created": created_ids,
            "parent_snapshot_hash": parent_snapshot_hash,
        },
        correlation_id=correlation_id,
    )
    session.flush()
    return AnalyzeResponse(
        jobs=[job_dto(j) for j in jobs],
        created=created_ids,
        dispatch=dispatches,
    )


def checkpoint_scope_project(session: Session, checkpoint: Checkpoint):
    from ..models import Project

    return session.get(Project, checkpoint.project_id)

@router.get("/answers/{answer_id}/input-packet", response_model=AnswerInputResponse)
def get_answer_input_packet(
    answer_id: str, principal: Principal = Depends(get_principal),
    session: Session = Depends(get_db),
) -> AnswerInputResponse:
    from packages.domain.hashing import canonical_json_sha256
    answer = scoped_answer(session, principal, answer_id)
    row = session.get(AnswerRequest, answer.request_id)
    if row is None or row.input_packet is None:
        raise ApiError("unavailable", "This historical answer has no frozen input packet", retryable=False)
    digest = canonical_json_sha256(row.input_packet)
    if digest != answer.provenance.get("input_packet_sha256"):
        raise ApiError("unavailable", "Frozen answer inputs failed integrity verification", retryable=False)
    return AnswerInputResponse(answer_id=answer.id, project_id=answer.project_id,
        snapshot_id=answer.snapshot_id, snapshot_hash=answer.snapshot_hash,
        context_hash=row.context_hash, selected_version_id=answer.selected_design_version_id,
        packet_sha256=digest, packet=row.input_packet)


@router.get("/capabilities", response_model=CapabilitiesResponse)
def get_capabilities(request: Request) -> CapabilitiesResponse:
    from ..services.analyzers import analysis_catalog
    from packages.perception.model_readiness import model_readiness
    caps = request.app.state.capabilities
    readiness = model_readiness("qwen").as_dict()
    guidance_modes = [
        {"mode": "template", "available": True, "optional": False,
         "availability_basis": "built_in", "reason": None,
         "detail": "Deterministic guidance over the selected evidence snapshot."},
        {"mode": "local_model", "available": readiness["available"] and not caps.fixture_mode,
         "optional": True, "availability_basis": readiness["availability_basis"],
         "reason": "fixture_mode" if caps.fixture_mode else readiness["reason"],
         "detail": "Local generation requires analysis mode." if caps.fixture_mode else readiness["detail"],
         "readiness": readiness},
    ]
    gate = deployment_gate_state(request.app.state.settings)
    gate["external_inference_enabled"] = caps.external_inference_enabled
    return CapabilitiesResponse(
        capabilities={**caps.as_dict(), "authentication_mode": request.app.state.settings.authentication_mode,
                      "synthetic_only": request.app.state.settings.authentication_mode == "dev_stub",
                      "analysis_analyzers": analysis_catalog(), "guidance_modes": guidance_modes},
        deployment_gate=gate,
        api_version="v1",
    )

def get_evidence(
    project_id: str,
    snapshot: str | None = None,
    principal: Principal = Depends(get_principal),
    session: Session = Depends(get_db),
) -> EvidenceResponse:
    """Evidence inventory for a snapshot; the newest snapshot when omitted."""
    project = scoped_project(session, principal, project_id, CAPABILITY_READ)
    current_hash = snapshots.current_snapshot_hash(session, project.id)

    if snapshot is not None:
        edges = snapshots.edges_for_snapshot(session, project.id, snapshot)
        if not edges:
            raise ApiError("not_found", "No such snapshot in this project")
        snapshot_id = snapshot
    else:
        edges = answer_service.evidence_rows_for_snapshot(session, project.id, None)
        snapshot_id = edges[0].snapshot_id if edges else ""

    # A served snapshot is current when its edge inventory equals the
    # project's active observations right now (supersessions change both).
    served_ids = {edge.observation_id for edge in edges}
    from ..services.consent import require_asset_use
    for edge in edges:
        observation = session.get(Observation, edge.observation_id)
        source = session.get(Asset, observation.asset_id) if observation is not None else None
        if source is not None:
            require_asset_use(session, source, "teaching_review")
    active_ids = set(
        session.execute(
            select(Observation.id).where(
                Observation.project_id == project.id, Observation.status == "active"
            )
        ).scalars()
    )
    is_current = bool(edges) and served_ids == active_ids

    return EvidenceResponse(
        project_id=project.id,
        snapshot_id=snapshot_id,
        current_snapshot_hash=current_hash,
        is_current=is_current,
        edges=[evidence_edge_dto(e) for e in edges],
    )

) -> ObservationListResponse:
    """Observation display records for the workbench evidence drawer.

    Superset of the active inventory: includes superseded/retracted records so
    the UI can render correction history; filter with ?status=active for the
    current-evidence view."""
    project = scoped_project(session, principal, project_id, CAPABILITY_READ)
    stmt = select(Observation).where(Observation.project_id == project.id)
    if status is not None:
        if status not in ("active", "superseded", "retracted"):
            raise ApiError("unprocessable_entity", "Unknown observation status filter")
        stmt = stmt.where(Observation.status == status)
    rows = session.execute(stmt.order_by(Observation.id)).scalars().all()
    from ..services.consent import require_asset_use
    for asset_id in {row.asset_id for row in rows}:
        source = session.get(Asset, asset_id)
        if source is not None:

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import time

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Request
from fastapi.responses import Response, StreamingResponse
from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from packages.domain.http_range import InvalidRange, parse_range

from ..authz import scoped_asset, scoped_job, scoped_project
from ..dependencies import get_db, get_object_store, get_principal

router = APIRouter()


@router.get("/assets/{asset_id}/content")
def get_asset_content(
    asset_id: str,
    request: Request,
    principal: "Principal" = Depends(get_principal),
    session: Session = Depends(get_db),
    store: ObjectStore = Depends(get_object_store),
):
    """Serve asset bytes with single-range support (206/416).

    Authorization is resolved before any byte is read; deleted assets answer
    404 so purged media stays inaccessible (docs/04).
    """
    asset = scoped_asset(session, principal, asset_id, CAPABILITY_READ)
    require_media_origin(request.app.state.settings, asset.origin)
    if asset.status != "active":
        raise ApiError("not_found", "No such asset in your scope")
    if not store.exists(asset.stored_key):
        raise ApiError(
            "unavailable",
            "Stored content is temporarily unavailable",
            retryable=True,
        )
    data = store.open(asset.stored_key)
    size = len(data)
    headers = {
        "Accept-Ranges": "bytes",
        "ETag": f'"sha256-{asset.sha256}"',
        "Cache-Control": "private, max-age=0, must-revalidate",
        "X-Content-Type-Options": "nosniff",
    }
    range_value = request.headers.get("range")
    try:
        byte_range = parse_range(range_value, size)
    except InvalidRange as exc:
        if exc.satisfiable:
            raise ApiError(
                "range_not_satisfiable",
                "Requested range is outside the asset",
                status=416,
                retryable=False,
            ) from exc
        raise ApiError("unprocessable_entity", "Malformed Range header") from exc

    if byte_range is None:
        headers["Content-Length"] = str(size)
        return Response(content=data, media_type=asset.mime_type, headers=headers)
    headers["Content-Range"] = f"bytes {byte_range.start}-{byte_range.end}/{size}"
    headers["Content-Length"] = str(byte_range.length)
    return Response(
        content=data[byte_range.start : byte_range.end + 1],
        status_code=206,
        media_type=asset.mime_type,
        headers=headers,
    )


@router.get("/assets/{asset_id}/derivatives", response_model=list[DerivativeResponse])
def list_derivatives(
    asset_id: str,
    request: Request,
    principal: "Principal" = Depends(get_principal),
    session: Session = Depends(get_db),
) -> list[DerivativeResponse]:
    """List derivatives of an asset (thumbnails, keyframes, transcripts).

    Phase 01 generates none; the AV phases populate this table with the same
    scope and privacy constraints as the source asset.
    """
    asset = scoped_asset(session, principal, asset_id, CAPABILITY_READ)
    require_media_origin(request.app.state.settings, asset.origin)
    rows = (
        session.query(AssetDerivative)
        .filter(
            AssetDerivative.asset_id == asset.id,
            AssetDerivative.project_id == asset.project_id,
        )
        .order_by(AssetDerivative.created_at, AssetDerivative.id)
        .all()
    )
    return [derivative_dto(row) for row in rows]


@router.get("/assets/{asset_id}/derivatives/{derivative_id}/content")
def get_derivative_content(
    asset_id: str, derivative_id: str, request: Request,
    principal: Principal = Depends(get_principal),
    session: Session = Depends(get_db), store: ObjectStore = Depends(get_object_store),
):
    asset = scoped_asset(session, principal, asset_id, CAPABILITY_READ)
    require_media_origin(request.app.state.settings, asset.origin)
    derivative = session.scalar(select(AssetDerivative).where(
        AssetDerivative.id == derivative_id, AssetDerivative.asset_id == asset.id,
        AssetDerivative.project_id == asset.project_id,
    ))
    if asset.status != "active" or derivative is None:
        raise ApiError("not_found", "No such derivative in your scope")
    if not store.exists(derivative.stored_key):
        raise ApiError("unavailable", "Stored derivative is temporarily unavailable", retryable=True)
    data = store.open(derivative.stored_key)
    import hashlib
    if hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest() != derivative.sha256:
        raise ApiError("unavailable", "Stored derivative failed integrity verification", retryable=False)
    return Response(content=data, media_type=derivative.mime_type, headers={
        "ETag": f'"sha256-{derivative.sha256}"', "Content-Length": str(len(data)),
        "Cache-Control": "private, no-store", "X-Content-Type-Options": "nosniff",
    })

@router.get("/projects/{project_id}/jobs", response_model=JobListResponse)
def list_project_jobs(
    project_id: str,
    principal: "Principal" = Depends(get_principal),
    session: Session = Depends(get_db),
) -> JobListResponse:
    """Read-only project job inventory (ADR 007 errata #3): the state-adaptive
    first screen derives 측정 중 / 검출 구간 없음 / 측정 일부 불가 from job
    history, so a never-analyzed project is never displayed as 검출 없음."""
    project = scoped_project(session, principal, project_id, CAPABILITY_READ)
    rows = list(
        session.execute(
            select(ProcessingJob)
            .where(ProcessingJob.project_id == project.id)
            .order_by(ProcessingJob.created_at.asc(), ProcessingJob.id.asc())
        ).scalars()
    )
    return JobListResponse(project_id=project.id, jobs=[job_dto(row) for row in rows])


def _sse_format(event: str, data: dict) -> str:
    return f"event: {event}\ndata: {json.dumps(data, sort_keys=True)}\n\n"


@router.get("/jobs/{job_id}/events")
def stream_job_events(
    job_id: str,
    request: Request,
    principal: "Principal" = Depends(get_principal),
    session: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Server-sent events for job progress (docs/03).

    Scope is checked before streaming; the stream polls persisted PostgreSQL
    state, because the database — not browser memory — is authoritative.
    """
    settings = request.app.state.settings
    job = scoped_job(session, principal, job_id)
    asset = scoped_asset(session, principal, job.asset_id)
    require_media_origin(settings, asset.origin)

    def event_stream():
        deadline = time.monotonic() + settings.sse_max_seconds
        yield _sse_format(
            "job",
            {
                "job_id": job.id,
                "state": job.state,
                "progress": job.progress,
            },
        )
        last_state = job.state
        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
            time.sleep(settings.sse_poll_seconds)
            with request.app.state.session_factory() as poll_session:
                current = poll_session.get(ProcessingJob, job.id)
                if current is None:  # pragma: no cover - concurrent tombstone
                    yield _sse_format("error", {"code": "not_found"})
                    return
                if current.state != last_state or current.progress != job.progress:
                    last_state = current.state
                    yield _sse_format(
                        "job",
                        {
                            "job_id": current.id,
                            "state": current.state,
                            "progress": current.progress,
                            "failure_code": current.failure_code,
                        },
                    )
                if current.state in ("succeeded", "partial", "failed", "canceled"):
                    yield "event: done\ndata: {}\n\n"
                    return
        yield _sse_format("timeout", {"reason": "sse_max_seconds_elapsed"})

    return StreamingResponse(
        event_stream(),
        media_type="text/event-stream",
        headers={"Cache-Control": "no-store", "X-Accel-Buffering": "no"},
    )

@router.post("/classrooms", response_model=ClassroomResponse, status_code=201)
def create_classroom(
    payload: ClassroomCreate,
    request: Request,
    principal: Principal = Depends(get_principal),
    session: Session = Depends(get_db),
) -> ClassroomResponse:
    """Dev bootstrap: create a classroom with the caller as its teacher.

    Production classroom provisioning is an administrative flow outside
    Phase 01; this exists so a local run needs no seeding script.
    """
    if principal.via == "capture_token":
        raise ApiError("not_found", "No such classroom in your scope")
    if request.app.state.settings.authentication_mode == "research_session":
        teacher = session.scalar(select(Membership.id).where(
            Membership.principal_id == principal.principal_id, Membership.role == "teacher",
        ).limit(1))
        if teacher is None:
            raise ApiError("forbidden_scope", "Classroom provisioning requires an existing teacher membership")
    classroom = Classroom(id=new_id("classroom"), name=payload.name.strip())
    session.add(classroom)
    session.add(
        Membership(
            id=new_id("membership"),
            classroom_id=classroom.id,
            principal_id=principal.principal_id,
            role="teacher",
        )
    )
    session.flush()
    return ClassroomResponse(id=classroom.id, name=classroom.name)

    A fresh browser renders the home screen from this alone — existence is
    never a per-browser localStorage fact. A capture token has no classroom
    scope, so it gets an empty list rather than an error."""
    if principal.via == "capture_token":
        return ClassroomListResponse(classrooms=[])
    rows = session.execute(
        select(Classroom)
        .join(Membership, Membership.classroom_id == Classroom.id)
        .where(Membership.principal_id == principal.principal_id)
        .order_by(Classroom.created_at, Classroom.id)

    return ClassroomListResponse(classrooms=[ClassroomResponse(id=row.id, name=row.name) for row in rows])

    payload: ProjectCreate,
    principal: Principal = Depends(get_principal),
    session: Session = Depends(get_db),
    correlation_id: str = Depends(get_correlation_id),
) -> ProjectResponse:
    if principal.via == "capture_token":
        raise ApiError("not_found", "No such project in your scope")
    membership = session.execute(
        select(Membership).where(
            Membership.classroom_id == payload.classroom_id,
            Membership.principal_id == principal.principal_id,

    ).scalar_one_or_none()
    if membership is None or membership.role != "teacher":
        # Classroom existence is not disclosed to non-members.
        raise ApiError("not_found", "No such classroom in your scope")
    project = Project(
        id=new_id("project"),
        classroom_id=payload.classroom_id,
        name=payload.name.strip(),
        status="active",
    )
    session.add(project)
    session.flush()
    session.add(
        ProjectAccess(
            id=new_id("project_access"),
            project_id=project.id,
            principal_id=principal.principal_id,
            role="teacher",
        )
    )
